⚠️ Breaking changes and upgrade notes

  • Host-only settings: Repository .pr_agent.toml files can no longer override GitHub pacing and retry settings (github.seconds_between_requests, github.seconds_between_writes, github.api_retries, github.ratelimit_retries), config.num_retries, azure_devops_server.agent_identity, custom-label settings (config.enable_custom_labels and [custom_labels]), or pr_code_suggestions.max_number_of_calls. config.num_retries is capped at 10. Per-directory .pr_agent.toml files also cannot set pr_code_suggestions.dual_publishing_score_threshold. Move values you rely on to host configuration. (#4445, #4475, #4485, #4632, #4745)
  • Comment arguments: config.ai_timeout and pr_code_suggestions.max_number_of_calls can no longer be set through command comments. (#4445)
  • Removed no-op settings: pr_code_suggestions.approve_pr_on_self_review and pr_code_suggestions.fold_suggestions_on_self_review are removed from the shipped configuration. PR-Agent warns if they remain set; they never changed /improve behavior. (#4598)
  • Custom provider integrations: Unused provider methods and capability names were removed. Review #4691 if a custom provider calls those internal methods.
  • Auto-approval: config.enable_auto_approval is now host-only. The auto-approval path remains disabled in this release. (#4700)

🔐 Trusted Publishing

PyPI releases now use PyPI Trusted Publishing through GitHub Actions OIDC and produce package attestations. The release workflow rejects commits that are not reachable from main. (#3909)

entry.title: v0.49.0
entry.content:
⚠️ Upgrade notes

  • GitHub polling needs an allowlist. New host-only github.polling_repositories = ["owner/repo", ...]; empty (the default) ignores every notification, so polling deployments must set it (#4294).
  • Jira project_keys = [] now disables lookups. The default is now ["*"]. If you set [] to mean "all projects", change it to ["*"] or remove it (#4049).
  • litellm.extra_headers is host-only. Repository .pr_agent.toml and comment arguments can no longer set it (#4287).
  • Default model is now gpt-6.1-sol with gpt-6-luna as fallback (was gpt-5.6 / gpt-5.6-terra). Pin config.model to keep the old one (#4088).
  • Langfuse SDK 4.18.0 needs self-hosted Langfuse 3.63.0+; use the langfuse_otel callback (#4343).
  • GitHub App token in Actions: set github.agent_login to <app-slug>[bot] so PR-Agent recognises its own comments (#4329).

✨ Highlights

  • pr-agent doctor preflights a deployment (#4321).
  • --json-output for /describe, /improve and /review (#4265, #4227, #4226).
  • Jira scoped API tokens (#4250), /ask with the CI artifact as context (#4176), globs in repo_context_files (#4220), opt-in GitLab subgroup settings inheritance (#4059).
  • Security hardening: DNS rebinding block, repo-context path escapes, host-only config output, loguru diagnose off, more credential redaction (#4252, #4279, #4293, #4280, #4328).

What's Changed

  • Redact Stripe, Twilio and SendGrid credentials by @IlyaKhalafi in #4328
  • ci(review): make self-hosted /improve post suggestions again by @Yoel-qin in #4174
  • Enable automatic /review on new PRs (fixes #4162) by @kiranmutyala18 in #4170

🚀 Features

⚠️ Breaking Changes

Warning

This release changes several defaults and makes more settings host-only. Check each item below against your deployment before upgrading.

  • pip install pr-agent no longer installs the git provider SDKs (#3679): PyGithub, python-gitlab, atlassian-python-api, the Azure DevOps SDKs, boto3, giteapy, the Google Cloud SDKs and a2a-sdk moved to the github, gitlab, bitbucket, azure, codecommit, gitea, google and mosaico extras. Install the ones you use, for example pip install "pr-agent[github]", or pr-agent[all] for the previous set. The Docker images already install all.
  • Docker service images run as a non-root user (#3910): the webhook, app, polling and Mosaico targets run as UID/GID 10001 with HOME=/home/pragent. Mounted secrets must be readable by that user, output and database directories must be writable, and home-relative mounts should move to /home/pragent. The GitHub Action, CLI and Lambda images still run as root.
  • Azure DevOps and Bitbucket Server webhooks require credentials (#3911): with azure_devops_server.webhook_username/webhook_password or bitbucket_server.webhook_secret unset, every webhook is rejected with HTTP 403. Set them on both the sender and PR-Agent before upgrading.
  • GitLab webhooks backed by a secret provider need a new token format (#3913): when GitLab credentials come from AWS Secrets Manager or Google Cloud Storage, the webhook's Secret Token must be <secret-name>:<webhook-token>. Name-only tokens are rejected with HTTP 401, so update the webhooks when you deploy.
  • Namespace-wide settings are off by default (#3908): PR-Agent no longer applies <namespace>/pr-agent-settings to every repository automatically. Set the host-only config.global_settings_repo = "pr-agent-settings" to keep the old behaviour.
  • [tool.pr-agent] in pyproject.toml is no longer read (#3941): move those settings to .pr_agent.toml.
  • More settings are host-only (#3840, #3904, #3950, #4001, #4054): a repository's .pr_agent.toml and comment arguments can no longer set provider endpoints (openai.api_base and the other api_base keys), keys ending in url, endpoint, org, key, token or secret, provider auth mode and TLS settings (github.deployment_type, gitlab.auth_type/ssl_verify, bitbucket.auth_type, gitea.skip_ssl_verification/ssl_ca_cert), jira.jira_site/jira_api_email/project_keys, or LiteLLM callbacks. They are ignored with a warning, so set them in host configuration instead. Comment arguments are restricted further as well (#3902).
  • Gitea and Gerrit read repository settings from the target branch (#3906): Gitea uses the PR base and Gerrit the default branch, so a .pr_agent.toml change inside a PR no longer applies to that PR.
  • Cross-repository reads need an allowlist (#3922, #3897): GitHub ticket context only reads linked issues and sub-issues from the PR's own repository or same-owner repositories listed in config.repo_context_sibling_repos. gitlab.expand_submodule_diffs only expands submodules listed there that sit in the MR's top-level group.
  • Ignore rules now cover comment commands (#3943): config.ignore_pr_authors, ignore_pr_labels, ignore_pr_title, the branch rules and ignore_repositories now skip manually triggered commands too, not only automatic ones.
  • merge_recommendation values were renamed (#4010): with pr_reviewer.require_merge_recommendation on, safe_to_merge is now no_concerns_found and merge_with_caution is now needs_review. changes_required is unchanged. Update anything that parses review output.
  • /describe comments no longer repeat the PR description (#4118): with pr_description.publish_description_as_comment = true, the comment leaves out the User Description section even when add_original_user_description is on, because the PR body is left untouched.
  • Smaller behaviour changes: webhook servers reject request bodies over 5 MiB with HTTP 413 (config.max_webhook_request_body_bytes, #3820). A positive config.max_output_tokens below 4096 is raised to 4096 (#4013). /describe and /generate_labels drop model labels outside the PR types and enabled custom labels (#3899).

⚠️ Important Changes

  • Gitea webhooks now require a secret (#3637): with gitea.webhook_secret unset, the Gitea app rejects every webhook with HTTP 403 instead of accepting it unsigned. Set the secret on the Gitea webhook and in your config before upgrading.
  • The GitHub Action fails on tool errors (#3712): a tool failure that used to be logged and swallowed now fails the Action. Set github_action_config.fail_on_tool_errors = false to keep the old green behaviour.
  • Comment commands need a leading / on GitLab, Bitbucket and Bitbucket Server (#3769): a comment only runs a tool when it starts with a slash command, so plain comments that mention one no longer trigger anything.
  • extra_config_url is host-only (#3638): a repository's .pr_agent.toml can no longer set it. Configure it on the host instead, for example with PR_AGENT_EXTRA_CONFIG_URL.
  • commitable_code_suggestions is now committable_code_suggestions (#3749): the old spelling still works with a deprecation warning until 1.0.
  • The Bitbucket Server webhook image runs under gunicorn (#3667): the container now starts multiple workers through the shared gunicorn_config.py instead of a single Python process.

Known issue: Bedrock Kimi K3, new in this release (#3651), still receives a temperature by default, which Bedrock is reported to reject. Until #3752 lands, add the model ids to config.no_temperature_models.

entry.content:
⚠️ Important Changes

  • GitHub App webhooks now require a configured secret (#2595): get_body() no longer accepts unsigned webhooks — a deployment without GITHUB.WEBHOOK_SECRET set is rejected with HTTP 403 instead of trusting every caller. Set the secret on your GitHub App and in your config before upgrading. The same PR escapes attacker-controlled webhook fields that were interpolated into CLI command strings.
  • Dependency management migrated to uv (#2509): requirements.txt, requirements-dev.txt, and the legacy setup.py are gone — dependencies now live in pyproject.toml with a committed uv.lock. Set up a dev environment with uv sync and run tools via uv run. Optional features are now extras (lambda, langchain — uv sync --extra <name>) or a dependency group (similar-issue — uv sync --group similar-issue), and Docker images install from the lockfile with uv sync --frozen. Installing from PyPI with pip install pr-agent still works.
  • Linting consolidated on Ruff (#2880): flake8 and the standalone isort pre-commit hook were removed. Contributors should run uv run ruff check --fix on touched files before committing.
